facts.statement: Phantomosaurus was discovered in 1965 and formally named in 1997 by Sander.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 1965 and named in 1997 as a species of Shastasaurus by Sander in the rocks of the Upper Muschelkalk.

facts.statement: Fossils of Phantomosaurus have been found in southern Germany.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in southern Germany.

facts.statement: The braincase of Phantomosaurus was studied by Maisch and Matzke in 2005.
facts.quote: More recently, in 2005, the braincase was studied by Maisch and Matzke.

facts.statement: Phantomosaurus possesses a very primitive braincase that resembles other diapsids more than other ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Phantomosaurus appears to have a very primitive braincase which resembles other diapsids more than other ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: Phantomosaurus is known from a partial skull, lower jaw, vertebrae, ribs, and hind fin.
facts.quote: Phantomosaurus is known from a partial skull, the lower jaw, some of the vertebrae and ribs (pictured) and the hind fin.

facts.statement: The hind fin of Phantomosaurus is very long and slender, featuring elongated femur, tibia, and fibula.
facts.quote: The hind fin is very long and slender, with elongated femur, tibia and fibula.

facts.statement: The limb structure of Phantomosaurus suggests it was long but not particularly powerful, generating a reasonable amount of lift.
facts.quote: These features suggest a long but not particularly powerful limb, which would have generated a reasonable quantity of lift.

facts.statement: The anterior centrum of each vertebra in Phantomosaurus has two symmetrical hollows, possibly to aid buoyancy.
facts.quote: The anterior centrum of each vertebra has two symmetrical hollows in, possibly to aid buoyancy.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Phantomosaurus is around 40 cm long and contains many conical teeth used for spearing fish.
facts.quote: The lower jaw is around 40 cm long and has many conical teeth for spearing fish.

facts.statement: The skull of Phantomosaurus is mostly disarticulated, with preserved bones including the quadratojugal, postfrontal, supratemporal, postorbital, basioccipital, parabasisphenoid, otic capsule, exoccipital, supraoccipital, and pterygoid.
facts.quote: The skull is mostly disarticulated. Bones we have found are: left quadratojugal, postfrontal, supratemporal, postorbital, basioccipital and both tubera basioccipitalia, the parabasisphenoid, the otic capsule containing both opisthotic and prootic bones, exoccipital, supraoccipital and pterygoid.

facts.statement: The quadratojugal of Phantomosaurus is very similar in shape to those of other large cymbospondylid ichthyosaurs, supporting its classification within that group.
facts.quote: This is very similar in shape to the quadratojugals of other large cymbospondylid ichthyosaurs, hence its classification as related to them.

facts.statement: In Phantomosaurus, the postorbital bone does not contact the upper temporal fenestra, unlike in many other ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: The postfrontal and supratemporal together form the border of the upper temporal fenestra, but unusually, the postorbital has no contact with this fenestra.

facts.statement: The basal plate of the parabasisphenoid in Phantomosaurus has a length of 27 mm, though its actual width cannot be measured due to preservation.
facts.quote: The basal plate was wider than its length of 27 mm, but the actual width cannot be measured as the right pterygoid is still articulated in the natural position.

facts.statement: The paraoccipital process of the opisthotic in Phantomosaurus is unusually long for an ichthyosaur, measuring around 25 mm.
facts.quote: The paraoccipital process is unusually long for an ichthyosaur, around 25 mm, but the entire opisthotic is only 38 mm long.

facts.statement: No other ichthyosaur possesses the feature where the foramen metoticum is completely enclosed by the exoccipital and opisthotic bones.
facts.quote: No other ichthyosaur has this feature.

facts.statement: The dorsal surface of the supraoccipital in Phantomosaurus features two thick ossifications that are not part of the parietal bone.
facts.quote: The most unusual feature was that the dorsal surface also had two thick ossifications, with smooth surfaces and wide bases, which cannot be part of the parietal bone.

facts.statement: Phantomosaurus had a concave condylus occipitalis.
facts.quote: The condylus occipitalis was concave.

facts.statement: Phantomosaurus had a paraoccipital process, a feature found in only one other ichthyosaur species, Shonisaurus.
facts.quote: A paraoccipital process is only present in one other ichthyosaur, Shonisaurus, but they are differently shaped.

facts.statement: Phantomosaurus retained postparietals, a primitive trait absent in other known ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Postparietals are not present on other known ichthtyosaurs, indicating this to be a plesiomorphy.

facts.statement: Phantomosaurus belongs to the parent group Cymbospondylidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Cymbospondylidae

facts.statement: Phantomosaurus is classified within the family Cymbospondylidae.
facts.quote: Family: Cymbospondylidae

facts.statement: Phantomosaurus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The genus Phantomosaurus was named by Maisch and Matzke in 2000.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Phantomosaurus (genus), Maisch and Matzke 2000

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Phantomosaurus has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
